title: Finite tensor-kernel tests detect factorization when the cokernel is finitely presented
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $U,V,W$ be $R$-modules, and $f:U\to V$ and $g:U\to W$ be $R$-linear maps. Suppose the quotient $V/f(U)$, namely the cokernel of $f$, is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. If for every finitely presented $R$-module $Q$ one has $\ker(f\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_Q)\subseteq\ker(g\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_Q)$ as submodules of $U\otimes_RQ$, then there is an $R$-linear map $h:V\to W$ with $g=h\circ f$. Tensor products and their induced maps are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No finite-generation, flatness or injectivity hypothesis on $U,V,W$ or $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 059D, lemma-domination, combined with Tag 059C, lemma-domination-fp: finite-presentation tests suffice for domination, and domination implies factorization when the cokernel of f is finitely presented.

proof.text: Put $C=V/f(U)$ and $\delta:U\to W\oplus V$, $\delta(u)=(g(u),-f(u))$. Define $P=(W\oplus V)/\delta(U)$, with quotient map $\rho$, and maps $a(w)=\rho(w,0)$, $b(v)=\rho(0,v)$. These are linear and $a\circ g=b\circ f$, since $\rho(g(u),-f(u))=0$. The map $p:P\to C$, $p(\rho(w,v))=[v]$, is well defined, linear and surjective: $-f(u)$ has zero class and every $[v]$ is $p(b(v))$. Moreover $\ker p=a(W)$. Indeed, $p(\rho(w,v))=0$ means $v=f(u)$ for some $u$, and the relation gives $\rho(w,v)=\rho(w+g(u),0)=a(w+g(u))$; conversely $pa=0$. Thus $W\xrightarrow{a}P\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$ is exact, with the given finitely presented module $C$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Tag 059D, lemma-domination, pushout construction and equality of cokernels; explicit quotient calculation as in Tag 0AUM, lemma-domination-universally-injective.

proof.text: For any $R$-module $Q$, abbreviate $f_Q=f\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q$ and similarly for other maps. From the bilinear universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] there are inverse linear maps $D:(W\oplus V)\otimes_RQ\to(W\otimes_RQ)\oplus(V\otimes_RQ)$ and $E$ given by $D((w,v)\otimes q)=(w\otimes q,v\otimes q)$ and $E(x,y)=(\iota_W\otimes1)(x)+(\iota_V\otimes1)(y)$. Here $\iota_W(w)=(w,0)$ and $\iota_V(v)=(0,v)$. The identities $DE=1$ and $ED=1$ follow on pure tensors from $(w,v)=(w,0)+(0,v)$, and then on all elements because pure tensors generate. Under this isomorphism $\delta_Q(z)=(g_Q(z),-f_Q(z))$ and $\rho_Q(E(t,0))=a_Q(t)$: each identity holds on pure tensors, hence everywhere.

source.place: Tag 0AUM, lemma-domination-universally-injective, tensoring the explicit pushout; finite-sum comparison written from the tensor universal property.

proof.text: The quotient sequence $U\xrightarrow{\delta}W\oplus V\xrightarrow{\rho}P\to0$ is exact by construction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] with any finitely presented $Q$ to obtain $\ker\rho_Q=\operatorname{im}\delta_Q$. If $t\in W\otimes_RQ$ has $a_Q(t)=0$, step 2 gives $E(t,0)\in\ker\rho_Q$, so $E(t,0)=\delta_Q(z)$ for some $z\in U\otimes_RQ$. Applying $D$ gives $(t,0)=(g_Q(z),-f_Q(z))$. Hence $f_Q(z)=0$, and the hypothesis on this finitely presented $Q$ gives $g_Q(z)=0$. Thus $t=0$. This proves that $a_Q$ is injective for every finitely presented $Q$; no injectivity of $f$ or $\delta$ was assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AUM, lemma-domination-universally-injective, tensor-kernel calculation; Tag 059C, lemma-domination-fp, finite-test reduction performed on the pushout inclusion.

proof.text: The factor-swap maps $W\otimes_RQ\to Q\otimes_RW$, $w\otimes q\mapsto q\otimes w$, and their analogues for $P$ are inverse to the reverse swaps by the bilinear universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; they intertwine $a\otimes1$ and $1\otimes a$ on pure tensors. Thus step 3 verifies exactly the finitely presented tests of [lem-trf-universal-injective-finite-test] for $a:W\to P$. That node gives injectivity of $a\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q$ for every $Q$. Taking $Q=R$ also makes $a$ itself injective, using $M\otimes_RR\cong M$, $m\otimes r\mapsto rm$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Tensor right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], now applied to the exact sequence of step 1 for each $Q$, gives exactness and surjectivity at the other two terms. Consequently $0\to W\xrightarrow{a}P\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$ is universally exact.

source.place: Tags 058K (theorem-universally-exact-criteria), finite tests, and 059D (lemma-domination), universal exactness of the pushout inclusion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-universally-exact-fp-split] with $A=W$, $B=P$, $i=a$ and the module $C=V/f(U)$. Step 1 gives $p$ surjective and $\ker p=a(W)$, step 4 gives injectivity and universal exactness, and the hypothesis gives finite presentation of $C$. Obtain an $R$-linear $r:P\to W$ with $ra=\mathrm{id}_W$. Put $h=r\circ b:V\to W$. The relation in step 1 gives $h\circ f=rbf=rag=g$. This is the required factorization.

source.place: Tag 059D, lemma-domination, application of Tag 058L (lemma-universally-exact-split) and the final pushout factorization.
